event: Property acquired with dry fissure and pipe
description: Phil Busick (Leslie Land Company LLC) acquired the Lower Sinter Terrace property (parcel 017-301-28) with the main fissure and an existing pipe sticking up out of the ground next to the main house -- ~5-6 years before the June 2025 eruption, per the document's own relative dating.

description: Per Phil Busick, the main fissure and pipe had always been dry, though steam could occasionally be seen coming from them; people occasionally dropped rocks or other objects down the pipe.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

event: Water begins accumulating in Big Pool/Big Hole
description: Dave Lostlen (property manager) began to notice water accumulating in the 'Big Pool/Big Hole' at the north end of the fissure.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: The main fissure was filled with water, with either no bubbling or only occasional bubbling.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

event: New steam fumarole forms near resort parking lot
description: A new steam fumarole (later called the South Fumarole) began to form next to the parking lot of the Steamboat Hot Springs Resort.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: Sustained bubbling in the fissure begins (previously only occasional).
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: Channel 4 News ran a story on 'geysers' returning to south Reno; NBMG staff organized a site visit in the following weeks.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

event: NBMG/Channel 2 site visit; Driveway Spring begins boiling
description: NBMG and Channel 2 News visited the Busick Property and Steamboat Hot Spring Resort: sustained bubbling in the Fissure, no activity in the Pipe, Big Hole filled with water (no bubbling), warm asphalt along the fissure's strike under the driveway. A small hole in the driveway ('Driveway Spring') began actively boiling during the visit; the fissure then stepped over several meters to the N-NW. A small steam fumarole with fresh sulfur staining ('North Fumarole') was found at the edge of the driveway.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: Bubbling in the fissure subsided; water remained warm/hot with steam regularly visible, only occasional bubbling observed.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: Sustained bubbling and spouting resumed in the fissure 1-2 weeks before the geyser eruption. Gene Savoy (Hot Springs Resort) also reported recent 'fluctuations' in their well, details unclear.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

event: Geyser first observed by resident / NBMG notified
description: ~8:10 pm: a Brookside Mobile Home Park resident (east side of Steamboat Creek) reported a steam/water spout; Laura Ruud (GSN) and Jim Faulds (NBMG) responded and photographed/videoed jets of water and steam from the Pipe and bubbling in the fissure by ~9:15 pm. Washoe County Sheriff and the property manager coordinated to cordon off the area. Per on-site resident 'Joy': water began trickling from the pipe/fissure at ~12:30 pm, erupting (max height ~50 ft) by ~4 pm, pooling in her driveway.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

event: Geyser more energetic overnight, moderates by morning
description: Property manager reported the geyser was much more energetic overnight (spouting an estimated '100 feet in the air') but only ~20-30 feet by the morning of 6/2. Jim Faulds reported (3:08 pm) that geyser activity ceased at the site during the afternoon. Per 'Joy': activity ceased around mid-day, stopping suddenly 'like someone had turned it off.'
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

event: First post-eruption field notes; pLIBS sampling
description: NBMG staff (Nicole, Rachel) visited the property: well no longer spewing water (standing water ~2 ft down in the pipe, steam escaping, slight bubbling); red staining along the fissure north of the pipe (3 samples collected, tested 6/4 with pLIBS); new geyserite along the fissure just north of the well; area otherwise dry (perpetual spouter inactive); air temp ~87 deg F near the fissure. Long-time resident Joy reported a broader increase in fumarole activity across the property (steam from places that previously emitted little/none) and new grass growth in a previously bare area.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: ~10:30 pm: Dave Lostlen received a resident report that the geyser was active again; notified Jim Faulds and sent a short video to NBMG the next morning. Per 'Joy': she heard loud cracking/popping sounds around this time, marking the renewed eruption's onset; she judged the first (6/1) eruption may have been slightly stronger.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events

description: Griffin (NBMG), on site ~9:30-11:30 am: geyser from the Pipe spouting an estimated 8-12 m (bursts to ~18 m, drone-altitude estimate); fissure steaming along its full length with intense sulfur smell and staining intensifying (yellow to reddish-orange) toward the Pipe; Big Pool muddy but empty; driveway cracks more pronounced than 2024; Driveway Spring dry but hissing/steaming at 95.1 deg C; a new second set of tiny fumaroles ~30 m north of the original North Fumarole measured 95.8 deg C; a previously-unsurveyed small warm spring ~40-45 m south of a resident's house measured 40.0 deg C; no other significant steam vents/seeps found on a walk-around near the creek (though ground was generally muddy/soft after overnight rain). A long-time resident (43 years) reported never having seen anything like this activity before.
citation: NBMG Steamboat Springs Approximate Timeline of Events
